THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE  119

was not so fortunate; being caught between the wheels and the bed of the vehicle. By almost super-human efforts they got the animal free. It was necessary for Boggan's word to let them off if they could get the old Justice of the peace to let them off, which they succeeded in doing, but not without tears and the promising never to do it again; so it all quieted down. A close ride that was—not the best, reducing the buggy to splinters. A clear ride that was.

Old April Fool Tradition.—That the tradition of good, clean fun at April Fool's is not unexpected in a college community full of high spirits; this reminiscence of Mr. W. H. Parker, an ex-student, tells without surprise the following episodes:

Aunt Bet said, "Come on, girls, to the kitchen and I'll help you get ready."

Mrs. Prewitt put in a layer of cotton, and poured custard over it. One girl took a piece. We girls watched the boys to see the boys' expressions. They would "sew" away from us and make faces, grinning and make faces, grinning away from us and then faces getting bigger. Then Darrett caught on looking and made us kneel down and pray for forgiveness—(he always did that). There was to be some tall praying to keep from being expelled from college.

*Personal letter from Mrs. H. H. (Shel Boy) Noel, Dallas, Texas, July 26, 1938.
